Leagues
* Are there any differences in the four leagues? Unless a game is intended as a contest, the usual practice seems to be using multiple leagues only when new rules or features are introduced between leagues.

* The stub is missing for Leagues 2 and 4. (This point is irrelevant if the puzzle is changed back to a single league.)

The Goal
* Consider rewording the winning conditions to avoid duplicating the later Victory Conditions section, or at least changing "escape" to "move".

* Are you planning to make the puzzle source code publicly available? If so, please include the link. (This is optional.)

Rules
* As the statement is written in HTML, consider replacing ALL CAPS ("OVER", "EXCEPT") with another style for emphasis.

* Official rules PDF: Are all the official rules replicated exactly? If not, please list all deviations, e.g.

  • The official rules use the terms "black" and "white" instead of "Attackers" and "Defenders".

  • Point 10 (a full game is played in two sets) is irrelevant.

  • The concepts of a turn limit and score don't exist in the official rules.

* Official rules PDF: Please note that if important rules exist only in the file, the statement will become incomplete if the file becomes inaccessible. Consider making the statement self-contained.

* Before the Movement section, please define the coordinate system, including the location of the origin (0, 0), and the directions in which the x- and y-coordinates increase.

* Please specify whether every game starts from the standard initial position defined in the official rules.

* Capturing: The term "hostile pieces" isn't clearly defined. Consider adding "also" before "act", and inserting:

The opponent's pieces are hostile pieces.

* Does the throne act as a hostile piece for Attackers and Defenders under different circumstances as described in the official rules? If so, consider explaining that behaviour in the statement.

* Please define how score is calculated.

* Under what circumstances is a draw declared? Is it when both players have the same score after the turn limit? Please specify.

Input for one game turn
* role: Please format "0" and "1" using the <const> tag.

* Please add "space-separated" between "4" and "variables".

* owner: Please capitalise "attackers" and "defenders".

* pieceType: Please format "ATTACKER", "DEFENDER" and "KING" using the <const> tag.

* Optionally, provide the board state instead of a list of pieces, as this is often easier for players to visualise. See Minishogi ( https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/minishogi ) for an example. For instance, "A" = Attacker, "D" = Defender, "K" = King and "." = an empty square. If this approach is adopted, the Rules should also explicitly state that the Defenders control the King.

Output
* Please format "MOVE" using the <action> tag.

* Please format "x1", "y1", "x2" and "y2" using the <var> tag, and explain what they represent.

* Please format "3 1 3 0" using the <const> tag.

Thanks.

Here is Brandubh, an ancient Celtic board game and a fast-paced 7x7 variant of the famous Viking game Hnefatafl! 
I wanted a game with purely asymmetrical gameplay. But is that really a good idea? :O

I can't wait to read your comments! :)

Thank you so much for this very thorough review! 
I was thinking of using the leagues to provide a learning curve for players (random AI, then minimax), but if the CG standard is focused on a single league, that’s fine. (and easier for me!)

As for access to the referee, I was waiting for your initial feedback. 
I’ll keep you posted! :)
